# Checklist: security
<!-- Generated by /speckit.checklist -->
<!-- Branch: 003-paginas-publicas | Date: 2026-09-09 -->

This feature builds the product's **only unauthenticated surface**. Everything before it was
reached with a session; these six pages are reached by anyone, and the same read path serves
them all. That is why this checklist exists for a feature that adds no endpoint and no field.

Requirement *quality* checks, adjudicated against the merged implementation. Every `[ ]` carries
an **OPEN** rationale.

| ID | Check | Dimension | FR/US Ref | Status |
|----|-------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| CHK058 | Is the anonymous read path named as one function, rather than left as "read publicly"?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — FR-002 names `getPublicScopedPayload(host)` and forbids `payload`/`req.payload` by name, which is a rule a lint can hold. | [authorization] | FR-002, US1 | [x] |
| CHK059 | Does the spec state that the tenant comes from the host, not from anything the visitor can send?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes, and it is the whole design: there is no session to read a tenant from, so the host is the only input, resolved server-side. | [authorization] | FR-002, SC-002 | [x] |
| CHK060 | Is "only published content" stated in a form that covers direct access, not just listings?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — "including by direct slug" (FR-003), which is what the detail pages' 404 implements. | [authorization] | FR-003 | [x] |
| CHK061 | Does the spec require the 404 for a draft to be indistinguishable from the 404 for a missing document?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — US10's error case says it must not distinguish "exists but is a draft" from "does not exist", and the pages implement it by having no branch at all rather than by matching two responses. | [data-protection] | FR-003, US10 | [x] |
| CHK062 | Is the published-only predicate specified per collection, given `evento` has a different status set?<br>**Adjudicated:** **CLOSED 2026-09-09 by CLR-011.** § Notes for planning says the predicate differs on the calendar, but no FR states it — FR-003 says "only `status = publicado`" flatly. The implementation shipped that flat reading and cancelled events vanished; the predicate is now per-collection with `rascunho` excluded, asserted at the gate in both directions — and FR-003 now says so too, having said the thing that was wrong until CLR-011. | [authorization] | FR-003, FR-008 | [ ] |
| CHK063 | Does the spec bound what a public read may return, so a collection added later is not public by default?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes, and this is feature 002's deny-by-default path, which 003 consumes rather than weakens: an undeclared collection raises rather than serving. 003 added `publicList` as a **reason string**, not a boolean, so declaring one requires writing why. | [authorization] | FR-002, FR-003 | [x] |
| CHK064 | Are the media collections explicitly *not* publicly listable, so files are reachable only through published content?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — research.md states it and the plan forbids proposing otherwise. Reachability is the rule: a file is public exactly when a published document references it at depth 1. | [data-protection] | FR-012, FR-030 | [x] |
| CHK065 | Is the anonymous **write** — the download counter — called out as a write, rather than hidden inside "downloads are served"?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes. FR-012 says served *and counted*, *through the tenancy choke point*, so the one write an unauthenticated visitor can cause is named as one. | [authorization] | FR-012, US3 | [x] |
| CHK066 | Is that write bounded — is there anything stopping an anonymous visitor inflating a counter without limit?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN.** Nothing in the spec rate-limits it, and nothing in the implementation does. A loop over the download route increments `downloads` indefinitely, and the count is displayed. It is a vanity metric rather than a permission, which is why it is not urgent — but "counted" was never qualified, so nobody decided this. | [input-sanitization] | FR-012 | [ ] |
| CHK067 | Are URL parameters treated as hostile input, with a stated behaviour for values that are not in the vocabulary?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — US2's error case fixes it: an unknown category narrows to `TODOS` rather than erroring or filtering on the raw string, and `parseListingParams` validates against the organization's own vocabulary. | [input-sanitization] | FR-010, US2 | [x] |
| CHK068 | Does the spec say a page may not name a tenant, a status or a page size, so a page cannot widen its own read?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes, in plan § Sketch 1, and it survived contact: the filter seam added in run 5 is an **allowlist** of content fields, so a page still cannot name any of the three, and an undeclared key raises rather than being ignored. | [authorization] | FR-002 | [x] |
| CHK069 | Is the isolation harness required to cover the anonymous vantage point specifically, not just "cross-tenant"?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — FR-026 names it, and `public-path` is its own matrix leg with its own mutation proof, run against this feature's change to the predicate. | [authorization] | FR-026, SC-011 | [x] |
| CHK070 | Does the spec require the harness to be **watched failing** on that vantage point, not merely to exist?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — SC-011 and the `Isolation harness can fail (public-path)` job, which was advisory until 2026-09-09 and is now a required status check. | [authorization] | FR-026, SC-011, SC-012 | [x] |
| CHK071 | Does any requirement leak an internal identifier to an anonymous visitor?<br>**Adjudicated:** **OPEN, narrowly.** Detail pages build download links as `/api/{collection}/{id}/download/{midiaId}`, so numeric row ids of both the content and the media are in public HTML. Both ids come from a document the visitor is already entitled to read and the route re-checks reachability, so this is enumeration surface rather than a leak — but the spec never considered it, and slugs were chosen for exactly this reason elsewhere. | [data-protection] | FR-012, FR-030 | [ ] |
| CHK072 | Is user-supplied content rendered as data rather than markup?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — the rich text is Lexical JSON through Payload's own converter, never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; grepping the app tree finds no occurrence. | [input-sanitization] | FR-030 | [x] |
| CHK073 | Does the spec say what a visitor may *not* do, rather than only what they may?<br>**Adjudicated:** yes — CLR-005 excludes signed-in state entirely, FR-016 removes the publish CTAs, and FR-013 states the absence of progress as correct rather than missing. | [authorization] | CLR-005, FR-013, FR-016 | [x] |
